## Description

Planktonic pennate diatom of lakes: needle cells (~60 × 3 µm) without a raphe (it does not glide),
joined by their posterior poles with mucilage pads into star-shaped colonies of ~8 cells. Very
efficient at low phosphorus: in Tilman's (1977) experiments it wins when P limits.

## In the simulation

<!-- GENERATED:presence -->
Drops: `pond` (weight 0.15), `puddle` (weight 0.15); 20 individuals in a reference drop at weight 1.
<!-- /GENERATED -->

A [star colony](../../mechanics/stalks-and-colonies.md) (`[being.star_colony]`), seeded in colonies and growing
by division. Cells are a bit wider (6 µm) so the soft body is stable. Si, P limited (Droop) with the
growth half-saturations of Tilman and Kilham. Host of chytrids.

## Literature

- Tilman D. (1977) Resource competition between planktonic algae: an experimental and theoretical
  approach. Ecology 58: 338–348.
- Tilman D., Kilham S.S. (1976) Phosphate and silicate growth and uptake kinetics of the diatoms
  *Asterionella formosa* and *Cyclotella meneghiniana* in batch and semicontinuous culture.
  J. Phycol. 12: 375–383 (µmax and K, **not verified** against the paper).

## Not implemented yet

- The constants of Tilman & Kilham are not verified (roadmap B).
- Real cells are ~3 µm wide.
- No sinking (no vertical axis).

## Unique and shared mechanics

Validated in the [Tilman experiment](../../mechanics/well-mixed-culture.md) against *Cyclotella* (batch and
chemostat). Shares the [frustule and Si limitation](../../mechanics/metabolism-and-nutrients.md) with every diatom;
the star colony is unique to it.
